<a id="how-and-why-to-do-translation-plus-clir-drills"></a>

## How and Why to Do Translation Plus CLIR Drills

[Captured source](<../../raw/sources/old-obsidian-vault-2026-10-07/Clippings/loophole-online/training-camp/translation/How and Why to Do Translation Plus CLIR Drills • LO.md>) · SHA-256 `28551070f63aea60181ca2eadf1163e07d65665fd720e5e483e6f713e5340503`

**Use boundary:** This is an attributed source explanation. Verify logical inferences independently and use current Joshua curriculum for student-facing delivery; source anecdotes and mechanism claims are not independently established.

##### Ellen's Notes

***Translation + CLIR Drills***

1. Read and translate the stimulus in chunks.
2. Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.
3. Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.
4. Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

***Translation + CLIR Drill Tips***

- Perform all steps of the drill out loud, and record your drills with a voice recorder.
	- You will eventually transition this process to silent, but the time goals are built around an outloud process.
- Press "record" at the very beginning, and do not end the recording until you have finished with the entire drill.
- Do not pause or stop the recording between steps or stimuli.
- No hyperskipping on Translation + CLIR Drills.

***Translation + CLIR Goals***

- The time goal for Translation + CLIR is 20 minutes.
- The accommodated time goal for Translation + CLIR is 30 minutes (or 25 minutes as an ideal stretch goal).
- Meeting this time goal is only valid under two conditions:
	- You have a legitimate CLIR for every stimulus.
		- You have translated and quipped every stimulus in the section.

- 0:31And now there's a big black hole in the middle of the sentence and the stuff on the edge of the word you don't know is now being encompassed by it as like, oh, well, I just don't know what that means.
- 0:39I'm, and I don't know that word, so I'm not going to know what it means. And what they want to do is keep on reading, just blowing past this word they don't know, and hoping that later on the rest of the text will help me understand what that word meant.
- 0:53So let me tell you why this doesn't work and why it's harmful. Because when you allow that word you don't know to permeate and become this big black hole that like, oh, I didn't know that word, so now I don't know anything really surrounding it either, there tends to be an avoidant mentality
- 1:09that accompanies that. That people generally feel uncomfortable acknowledging that there is a word they don't know in the moment and so they don't really want to sit in that kind of icky, uncomfortable feeling and so they want to move forward. They want to get away from it.
- 1:23And they tell themselves this little white lie of, oh, I'm keeping on going because I don't have time to know what this means and reading more, maybe it'll help me know what it means.
- 1:32The truth of the matter is you do not actually go back to that word and figure out what it means.
- 1:36You just continue on and try and pretend that it isn't there. And the later paragraphs or whatever it is, they do not actually tell you what the word meant and you shouldn't pretend that actually going on is really in service of knowing what the word meant because it isn't

- 2:24that when you see that word, you're like, hmm, I'm not sure about that. OK, you're allowed to read like to the end of the sentence, the end of the thought for sure and then but when you get to the end of that sentence, I want you to go back and I want you to take an educated guess on what that

## Whats the Translation Standard Were Trying to Hit

[Captured source](<../../raw/sources/old-obsidian-vault-2026-10-07/Clippings/loophole-online/training-camp/translation/Whats the Translation Standard Were Trying to Hit • LO.md>) · SHA-256 `dcad8451d2e3bfb2d20a90318be2675c2ab49d33a435a389cfecf22969388185`

#### What's the Translation Standard We're Trying to Hit?

- 0:00What is the Translation standard we're trying to hit? You know, what does good look like? What is the Elysium at the end of the rainbow here?
- 0:07It is that when you read and translate a stimulus, you have a 100% conceptual awareness, 100% conceptual retention of all of the information that is presented to you in that stimulus.
- 0:19Now, that does not mean that you are literally reciting every word of the stimulus in the exact order it's given absolutely verbatim.
- 0:27You're totally free to translate into your own words using your own language and also to take things out of order.
- 0:35But when I say translate things in your own words, I don't mean take away the details. What I mean is save the details in your own words.
- 0:44And maybe that's fewer words because you're able to conceptualize the information in a more efficient way, but it actually covers all of the information.
- 0:52If that's so, that's totally fine. But I don't want you to take efficiency in your Translation as an excuse to leave information out
- 0:59because you need all the concepts in the stimulus to be retained and presented within your Translation. And you wanna retain your entire Translation as you're going into the answer choice because you need that information,
- 1:10that information interrelated with the information that's given to you in the answer choices is how you'll know what is correct and what is incorrect.
- 1:17But the standard isn't just conceptual retention and conceptual awareness, it's also the way in which that conceptual awareness is gained.
- 1:25Eventually what you want is for Translation and quipping to feel like breathing, feel like water, feel like something that you cannot turn off.
- 1:33It's just when you read, you are naturally translating without having to volitionally tell yourself that you have to translate. And without having to say, okay, I need to remember this, look for this, remember that, you just do remember it. That is the goal of mastery that we're
- 1:51hoping to achieve here. When I am going through and reading something, the reason why I didn't know Translation existed for so long is because I did not know that I was actually doing all of this.
- 2:00It was just that at the end of reading a stimulus, I'd of course be able to tell you everything that happened because I thought that was just the way people read.
- 2:08That's what we want for you is that as you're going through, all of these things are naturally happening in a subconscious way that form a great process that at the end of the stimulus, you're like, yeah, of course I know what it said.
- 2:18How could I not? Of course I know what it said. How could I not? Isn't that just such a gift of entitlement?
- 2:24Of course I know what it said. How could I not? That's the standard that we're going for at the end of every stimulus in logical reasoning at the end of every passage as well.
- 2:35All right, I'll see you soon.
